passage:
In the narrow bathroom of the family flat in Delhi, Jagdish pulled on his school shirt and thought, my stomach looks weird today. He stopped. What would he say if Preeti said this out loud? Probably, "You're fine, and we're late for chai."
So he said the same to himself, quietly, and left.
It was a bad body day, not a bad life. At the canteen Preeti waved him to the last free bench. "Rehearsal at four, don't forget." He hadn't thought of skipping it, and he didn't love his body that morning, but he didn't need to. Neutral was enough. He sat down with his tea and went to rehearsal later in his crumpled shirt.

qa.q: How did Jagdish feel about his body that morning, and what changed when he imagined Preeti saying the same words?
qa.a: He felt self-conscious about his stomach, but realising he would tell Preeti she was fine showed him how unkind he was being, and he settled into feeling neutral, which was enough.

qa.q: How did Jagdish treat the bad body day?
qa.a: He spoke to himself as he would to a friend, called it a bad body day, not a bad life, and carried on with his plans without needing to love his body. 🙂

qa.q: How might Preeti see Jagdish arriving in a crumpled shirt?
qa.a: Preeti probably just sees a friend showing up for rehearsal, and doesn't notice the shirt or the stomach at all.

grounding: Shows a teen on a bad body day speaking to himself as to a friend and going on with his plans.

passage:
'Go without me,' Hemant called through the bathroom door. 'My face is all puffy and this shirt looks terrible.'
'It's the final. We need our goalkeeper,' Asif said.
'I look like a balloon today.'
'You played the semi with a cold and saved two penalties.'
Silence. Hemant stood at the mirror, jaw tight. Then, almost to himself: 'If you'd said this about yourself, what would I tell you?'
'What?'
'I'd tell you it's one bad day. That your face doesn't catch the ball. That you're allowed to feel a bit rubbish and still show up.'
'...That's actually decent advice.'
Hemant breathed out slowly. 'I don't have to like how I look today. It can just be okay.'
He opened the door, gloves already in his hand.
'Ready?'
'Ready enough. Let's go.'

qa.q: What position does Hemant play for the team?
What was Hemant feeling as he stood at the mirror with his jaw tight?
qa.a: He felt self-conscious and low about his puffy face, tempted to skip the final.

qa.q: What small step helped Hemant move on with his plans?
qa.a: He asked what he'd tell a friend in his place, spoke to himself that kindly, and settled for 'okay' instead of perfect.

qa.q: How does Asif see Hemant's bad body day?
qa.a: He sees his goalkeeper, not a balloon, and just wants his friend on the pitch for the final 👍

grounding: Shows a teen on a bad body day speaking to himself as he would to a friend, settling for feeling okay and going ahead with his plans.

passage: The morning of Kalyani's birthday picnic last month, I nearly didn't go. I'd tried on four outfits and hated all of them; my stomach felt huge, my hair wouldn't sit, and I'd already typed 'sorry, fever' to cancel. Then I thought about what I'd say if Kalyani sent me that message about herself. I'd never tell her she looked awful. I'd say, 'Wear the comfy one and come, we just want you there.' So I said it to myself, out loud, feeling a bit silly in front of the mirror. I didn't suddenly love my stomach. I didn't need to. I just decided it was a normal body having a meh day. I deleted the message, put on the old green kurta and caught the bus. We played frisbee till sunset, and I barely thought about my stomach again. I'm Vinita, and I'm learning okay is enough.

qa.q: What message had Vinita typed to cancel the picnic?
How was Vinita feeling while trying on outfits that morning?
qa.a: Vinita felt low and self-critical, hating every outfit and ready to fake a fever to avoid going.

qa.q: What did Vinita try that turned the morning around?
qa.a: Saying out loud the kind words that would be offered to Kalyani, then settling for 'normal body, meh day' and going.

qa.q: What would Kalyani have missed if Vinita had sent that message?
qa.a: She would have missed a friend at her birthday picnic, when all she wanted was Vinita there, not a perfect outfit.

grounding: A first-person account of a bad body day where the narrator speaks to themself like a friend, settles for neutral and goes ahead with plans.
